Background — DURF Theme 3: Full Text Capture

This dashboard is a direct outcome of DURF (Dutch Repository Federation), Theme 3 – Full Text Capture. See the full roadmap on the DURF Gantt chart. It was built following discussions with the Theme leads for Theme 3 and Theme 2, Pascal and Rutger.

Goal
  • Comprehensive full-text availability in Dutch repository/CRIS systems, primarily to enhance preservation, and secondarily to enable text-mining, AI usage, and Taverne mechanisms.
  • Establish baseline metrics and a reporting system for full-text uptake.
Outcome
  • A Digital Sovereignty Health CRIS/Repo Dashboard: a chart with the ratio of metadata records containing a link to a file (PDF) on the institutional domain, per repository, over time.

Proof of concept, not a live connection: this dashboard does not query the DuckLake catalog live. Every figure was fetched once via a direct DuckDB connection to the public SURF ORI DuckLake catalog and embedded in this page as a static snapshot. If new data lands in the catalog afterwards — institutions depositing files, harvests re-running, metadata edits — none of that will appear here. The numbers will drift from the live catalog over time; treat this as a demonstration of what's possible, not a monitoring tool, until it's wired up to refresh automatically or rebuilt from a fresh extract.

Source: SURF ORI DuckLake, schema cris.publications. Data aggregated by institution × publication type × year × open access status × file status × license × publisher. Years 1995–2025 (2026 is still in progress).

Data currency: the cris.publications table in this catalog was last (re)loaded on 4 March 2026 (UTC, per the catalog's own snapshot log). Individual records also carry their own last-modified timestamp from the source repository (OAI-PMH header.datestamp), which ranges up to 15 April 2026 depending on the institution — see per-institution dates. Everything in this dashboard is a static snapshot as of those dates: if an institution deposits files, changes access rights, or otherwise edits records afterwards, that will not show up here until the catalog is reloaded and this dashboard is rebuilt from it.

Publishers: percentage with file

Normalized publisher names (variants merged), sorted from low to high. Only publishers with at least 100 publications in the current selection. "No publisher" and "Other publisher" (long tail, not normalized) are excluded here. Red = low coverage, green = high coverage — candidates for further investigation appear at the top.

File status is determined per publication: "Open file" if at least one file is publicly accessible (COAR c_abf2), otherwise "Embargoed file" if files exist but are all embargoed (c_f1cf), otherwise "No file". License is the first license of the first file; where file or license information is missing, this is shown separately. "Unknown" for open access status means: no ar:Access value in the source metadata. Publisher is the first name from cerif:Publishers, with common spelling variants (e.g. "Elsevier B.V.", "Elsevier Inc.", "Elsevier Ltd") merged into a single name; publications with no publisher field fall under "No publisher", less frequent publishers under "Other publisher".
